codex.chapter.aero_basics.intro.0: Create Aeronautics doesn't pretend. A structure here doesn't teleport between points — it flies: lists under weight, loses altitude when the burner dies, and crashes if the pilot forgot the ground is hard.
codex.chapter.aero_basics.intro.1: Two more mods come with it: Create Simulated — sensors, ropes, physical mechanisms — and Create Offroad, which puts it all on wheels.
codex.chapter.aero_basics.subtitle: Real physics, airships and levitite
codex.chapter.aero_basics.title: Create Aeronautics: Flight
codex.chapter.ca_electric.intro.0: The pack's three technologies speak different languages: Create in rotation, Immersive Engineering and Mekanism in energy. Create Addition is the translator. Without it three factories would stand side by side and never know of each other.
codex.chapter.ca_electric.subtitle: Turning rotation into energy and back
codex.chapter.ca_electric.title: Create Addition: Electricity
codex.chapter.cbc_advanced.subtitle: Steel, autocannons and special shells
codex.chapter.cbc_advanced.title: Big Cannons: Heavy Ordnance
codex.chapter.cbc_foundry.intro.0: Create Big Cannons is real artillery: barrels are cast from melt, bored, welded into sections, loaded with powder charges and shells, and block strength in the world truly counts on impact.
codex.chapter.cbc_foundry.intro.1: Metals ascend: cast iron, bronze, steel, nethersteel. Better metal, bigger charge the barrel takes.
codex.chapter.cbc_foundry.subtitle: Metals, molds and the first gun
codex.chapter.cbc_foundry.title: Big Cannons: Foundry
codex.chapter.create_andesite.intro.0: Andesite casing is a door. Behind it: press, millstone, saw and fan — four machines that already double ore, cut planks, grind flour and smelt a stream. Not a factory yet. But no longer a workshop.
codex.chapter.create_andesite.subtitle: First machines: press, millstone, saw, fan
codex.chapter.create_andesite.title: Andesite Age
codex.chapter.create_basics.intro.0: Create doesn't know the word 'energy'. It knows rotation: every shaft has speed and stress, and the whole art is adding one to the other so the machine doesn't stall.
codex.chapter.create_basics.intro.1: The first andesite alloy isn't a machine yet. It's a promise that in a few dozen hours your first train will leave from this very spot.
codex.chapter.create_basics.subtitle: Andesite alloy, shafts and sources of power
codex.chapter.create_basics.title: First Rotation
codex.chapter.create_brass.intro.0: Brass is the border between 'did it by hand' and 'did it once and for all'. Everything that filters, counts, chooses and decides needs it. Before brass Create is a set of clever gadgets; after — a factory.
codex.chapter.create_brass.subtitle: Brass, crushing wheels and smart automation
codex.chapter.create_brass.title: Brass Age
A contraption is a piece of the world that Create tears off and moves as one. A bridge that turns. A drill that drives. A house that spins on an axis if you felt like it. The rules are the same everywhere: assemble, apply rotation, let go.
codex.chapter.create_contraptions.title: Contraptions
codex.chapter.create_copper.intro.0: Copper is steam. Copper casing opens boilers, engines and the gear that lets you go where you couldn't before.
codex.chapter.create_copper.subtitle: Steam, pressure and diving
codex.chapter.create_copper.title: Copper Age
codex.chapter.create_fluids.intro.0: A pipe in Create stores nothing. It's only a path. Count tanks and pumps, not meters of line; and the first thing that surprises a newcomer is that water in a pipe doesn't flow by itself.
codex.chapter.create_fluids.subtitle: Pipes, pumps, valves and industrial pouring
codex.chapter.create_fluids.title: Fluids
codex.chapter.create_kinetics.intro.0: Speed in Create isn't free: faster means costlier in stress. This chapter is about the levers that turn, mute, accelerate and program rotation.
codex.chapter.create_kinetics.subtitle: Gearboxes, clutches, speed and its price
codex.chapter.create_kinetics.title: Controlling Rotation
codex.chapter.create_packages.intro.0: Create's sixth version brought the post. Items are packed into cardboard boxes, boxes ride chains and belts, and the stock answers orders without asking who ordered. There's something of an old post station in it — and something of a factory that knows what it's missing.
codex.chapter.create_packages.subtitle: Create 6 logistics: boxes, stock and orders
codex.chapter.create_packages.title: Packages and Factory
codex.chapter.create_tools.subtitle: Create tools and building from blueprints
codex.chapter.create_tools.title: Gear and Schematics
codex.chapter.create_trains.intro.0: A Create train doesn't ride the rails — it lives on them. It has a schedule, a conductor, signals that won't let two trains on one section, and a board it's awaited on at the station.
codex.chapter.create_trains.intro.1: The first line usually links base to mine. The last runs past the horizon just because it can.
codex.chapter.create_trains.subtitle: Tracks, stations, schedules and Steam 'n' Rails
codex.chapter.create_trains.title: Trains
codex.chapter.create_world.subtitle: Structures, decor and small add-ons
codex.chapter.create_world.title: Create in the World
codex.chapter.dim_aether.intro.0: Aether is a sky you can fall out of. Islands hang over the void, the light is soft, and gravity — if gravitite is to be believed — is negotiable. Three dungeons, three keys, three bosses — and the hammer it was all for.
codex.chapter.dim_aether.subtitle: The sky dimension: dungeons, gravitite and valkyries
codex.chapter.dim_aether.title: Aether
codex.chapter.dim_end.subtitle: The dragon, ender pearls and the way beyond
codex.chapter.dim_end.title: The End
codex.chapter.dim_nether.intro.0: The Nether here is vanilla. The place didn't change — demand did: blazes are needed by Create, quartz by Refined Storage, netherite by three mods at once. Every trip down now has a shopping list.
codex.chapter.dim_nether.subtitle: What the pack's mods take from the Nether
codex.chapter.dim_nether.title: The Nether
codex.chapter.dim_twilight.intro.0: The Twilight Forest is the pack's most orderly adventure. It won't let you further than you've earned: while the Naga lives, the Lich's tower is shut; while the Lich lives, the swamp and labyrinth poison and freeze. That's not a restriction — it's a map.
codex.chapter.dim_twilight.subtitle: A strict boss chain from the Naga to the Yeti
codex.chapter.dim_twilight.title: Twilight Forest
codex.chapter.end_apotheosis.intro.0: Three things hardest to do, and one that can't be done without doing everything else.
codex.chapter.end_apotheosis.subtitle: The book's last quests
codex.chapter.end_apotheosis.title: Apotheosis
codex.chapter.end_marathon.intro.0: No bosses and no builds here — only volume. Each quest is turned in with one press, but gathered only by a network that makes things itself. It's an autocraft test disguised as greed.
codex.chapter.end_marathon.subtitle: Numbers you can't catch without an autocraft chain
codex.chapter.end_marathon.title: Marathon
codex.chapter.end_monuments.intro.0: The pack's finale isn't a fight or an item. The finale is what stays standing when you log out. Every quest here demands product in amounts that can't be made by hand at all. Only a factory. Only automation.
codex.chapter.end_monuments.intro.1: Turn in — receive. And receive what speeds the next monument.
codex.chapter.end_monuments.subtitle: Builds that justify the whole factory
codex.chapter.end_monuments.title: Monuments
codex.chapter.et_amber.intro.0: A rich, bright, polite world that exiles the unwanted to Purgatorium and keeps in a labyrinth what isn't spoken of. The crystal needs level thirteen: pharos, illuminati fish, flame sphere, truadamantite, Crystal of Greatness.
codex.chapter.et_amber.subtitle: A bright dimension with a dark secret
codex.chapter.et_amber.title: Kingdom of Amber
codex.chapter.et_archaeology.subtitle: Brushes, blueprints, vases and totems
codex.chapter.et_archaeology.title: Archaeology
codex.chapter.et_comets.intro.0: Comets are pink-and-blue forests on rocks that should have fallen long ago. The mod's first dimension and its gentlest: here you can still make a mistake and live.
codex.chapter.et_comets.intro.1: The Comets crystal needs sorcery level two and five components: ancienzyte-framed bleedwood, inverted mud, terra crystal, grave dirt and a block of hyacinthum gold.
codex.chapter.et_comets.subtitle: First dimension: floating islands and the Terrible Tree
codex.chapter.et_comets.title: Comets
codex.chapter.et_darkness.subtitle: Hard mode and humanity
codex.chapter.et_darkness.title: Eternal Darkness
codex.chapter.et_eden.intro.0: After Purgatorium the light hurts. Here live the Sunfurry — messiahs, huscarls and warriors — and here they drank the Drink of the Sun until Volcanech came for the king.
codex.chapter.et_eden.intro.1: The Eden crystal needs level six: silver, two sunstone nuggets, dragon's breath and monster blindness.
codex.chapter.et_eden.subtitle: The sunny world of the Sunfurry
codex.chapter.et_eden.title: Gardens of Eden
codex.chapter.et_farming.subtitle: Pots, machines, nets and bug nets
codex.chapter.et_farming.title: Garden, Fishing and Catching
codex.chapter.et_gear.subtitle: Armors, weapons and artifacts
codex.chapter.et_gear.title: Eternal Tales Gear
codex.chapter.et_intro.intro.0: Eternal Tales begins quietly: with a journal, a town of musicians, a storyteller who knows more than he says. Nine dimensions come later — in the order someone else's war arranged them.
codex.chapter.et_intro.intro.1: The mod documents itself almost completely. Notice boards in Eternal Town explain every mechanic, and the journal keeps the quest list. This book only shows the order to read them in.
codex.chapter.et_intro.subtitle: Journal, Eternal Town and notice boards
codex.chapter.et_intro.title: Eternal Tales
codex.chapter.et_karvat.intro.0: An ancient place where gods still walk the earth and answer the altars' call. The crystal needs level eight: darkplasm, soulbone, comet crystal, spore edennus and crimson eel.
codex.chapter.et_karvat.subtitle: Divine forest and deities
codex.chapter.et_karvat.title: Lands of Karvat
codex.chapter.et_nether_end.subtitle: The Piglin Clocktower and the Ancient Chorus
codex.chapter.et_nether_end.title: Nether and End
codex.chapter.et_overworld.intro.0: Eternal Tales doesn't start with portals but with the old world ceasing to be familiar: blue cobalt appears in the rock, a red moon rises at night, and someone is digging a hive under the hill.
codex.chapter.et_overworld.subtitle: Ores, lunar events and first bosses
codex.chapter.et_overworld.title: The Overworld
codex.chapter.et_purgatorium.intro.0: This is where they exile. Nobody returns — so the Kingdom of Amber believes, and Heveline, living in a ruined house with a dying brother, doesn't argue.
codex.chapter.et_purgatorium.intro.1: The crystal needs sorcery level four: fire moss, skylite, lapsidian, aerolite and hellrock.
codex.chapter.et_purgatorium.subtitle: Darkness, the Rock Blaze and the Fallen Rune
codex.chapter.et_purgatorium.title: Purgatorium
codex.chapter.et_rayana.intro.0: Jungles where the night lasts longer than it should. The Aede tribe builds temples, the Daredian tribe hides in the mountains, and between them flies what brought the disease here.
codex.chapter.et_rayana.intro.1: The crystal needs level eight: darkplasm, soulbone, destroyer's eye, sunhog leather, nether fish.
codex.chapter.et_rayana.subtitle: Tropics, vampirism and Pterion
codex.chapter.et_rayana.title: Rayana
codex.chapter.et_skills.intro.0: Skills grow on their own — from what you do. Each new level of any of them gives a point you can put into any other via the board. So a digger becomes a sorcerer, and a sorcerer a fisherman if needed.
codex.chapter.et_skills.subtitle: Nine skills and level points
codex.chapter.et_skills.title: Skills
codex.chapter.et_sorcery.intro.0: Sorcery here is a craft. Runes drop from stones, stones stand in every world, and every world has its own rune. From runes brew essences, from essences — power.
codex.chapter.et_sorcery.subtitle: Runes, essences, matrix and astral enchanting
codex.chapter.et_sorcery.title: Sorcery
codex.chapter.et_ultimate.intro.0: After the end of the road there's one more world. Its crystal folds from Unahzaal, Rayana, Purgatorium, Karvat and the Ultimate Bricks, and in it live the Arkemers — a civilization whose machines make black holes tame.
codex.chapter.et_ultimate.subtitle: Arkemers, aetherium and the real endgame
codex.chapter.et_ultimate.title: Ultimate World
codex.chapter.et_unahzaal.intro.0: Unahzaal isn't a place. It's what remained when all the mod's worlds were joined into one. Its crystal is assembled from the crystals of Amber, Comets, Eden and Volcanech and needs sorcery level sixteen — more than anything before.
codex.chapter.et_unahzaal.intro.1: The main progression ends here. Everything after is for those not ready to stop.
codex.chapter.et_unahzaal.subtitle: The multiverse and the end of the road
codex.chapter.et_unahzaal.title: Unahzaal
codex.chapter.et_volcanech.intro.0: The world that started the war. From here came the destruction of Comets and the kidnapping of Eden's king; here too are those against it. The crystal needs level ten: ichor, tapinella, aragotium, beetle chitin, dark ichor.
codex.chapter.et_volcanech.subtitle: Volcanoes, aggression and betrayal
codex.chapter.et_volcanech.title: Volcanech
codex.chapter.fd_kitchen.intro.0: Farmer's Delight turns food into a system. Finished dishes give the Nourishment effect — hunger stops draining for a while, noticeably handier than vanilla steaks.
codex.chapter.fd_kitchen.subtitle: Farmer's Delight: knives, board, pot and skillet
codex.chapter.fd_kitchen.title: Kitchen
codex.chapter.final_bridges.intro.0: The pack's branches are self-sufficient, but it truly opens up at the seams. This chapter is a map of the crossings.
codex.chapter.final_bridges.intro.1: Every quest here needs items from several mods at once: that's the test of whether you've tied production together.
codex.chapter.final_bridges.subtitle: How three tech lines join into one
codex.chapter.final_bridges.title: Bridges Between Mods
codex.chapter.final_goals.intro.0: This pack has no single ending. It has ten, and none is mandatory. Below are the peaks of each branch. Reach them all — and you've seen everything here, and realized you've long been building your own game.
codex.chapter.final_goals.subtitle: How the pack ends
codex.chapter.final_goals.title: Final Goals
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.intro.0: Apotheosis rewrites the rules of loot. An ordinary iron sword from a chest may now turn out to be a 'Blazing Blade of Devastation' with three affixes and a gem socket — or it may stay an ordinary iron sword.
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.intro.1: The mod offers no progression in the usual sense. It offers a lottery you'll play for the rest of the pack, and the tools to tilt that lottery your way.
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.intro.2: It also lifts the enchanting ceiling: level thirty stops being the limit.
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.subtitle: Affixes, gems and gear that never repeats
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.title: Apotheosis
codex.chapter.hunt_beasts.intro.0: Three mods fill the world with the life vanilla was missing: from harmless capybaras to bosses you build an arena for.
codex.chapter.hunt_beasts.intro.1: Alex's Mobs is a hundred creatures with their own habits and useful drops. Mowzie's Mobs is four staged boss fights. Mutant Monsters is vanilla mobs allowed to grow up.
codex.chapter.hunt_beasts.subtitle: Alex's Mobs, Mowzie's Mobs and Mutant Monsters
codex.chapter.hunt_beasts.title: Beasts and Mutants
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.intro.0: L_Ender's Cataclysm adds no ores and no machines. It adds reasons to leave the house: eight enormous structures, each holding something that will kill you on the first attempt.
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.intro.1: There's no progression in the usual sense — there's an order by difficulty. You start in the Nether at the Soul Forge and finish on the Burning Arena, where Ignis waits.
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.intro.2: Boss weapons can't be crafted from anything else and have no equivalents. That's the whole point.
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.subtitle: Eight dungeons, eight bosses and weapons found nowhere else
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.title: Cataclysm
codex.chapter.ie_chemistry.subtitle: Plant oil, ethanol, biodiesel and polymers
codex.chapter.ie_chemistry.title: Chemistry and Fuel
codex.chapter.ie_gear.subtitle: Weapons, tools and armor
codex.chapter.ie_gear.title: Engineer's Gear
codex.chapter.ie_machines.subtitle: Crusher, press, arc furnace and excavator
codex.chapter.ie_machines.title: Multiblock Machines
codex.chapter.ie_power.intro.0: IE wires shock. Not figuratively: touch an uninsulated live wire and at best you get a scare. There's an honesty in it: a grid that can be built wrong is worth building right.
codex.chapter.ie_power.subtitle: Wires, voltages, generators and transformers
codex.chapter.ie_power.title: Power Grid
codex.chapter.ie_start.intro.0: Immersive Engineering doesn't hide its machines in one block. The coke oven is a three-by-three cube, the blast furnace another, the excavator a structure the size of a house. Everything here takes space, pulls cables and needs you walking around with a hammer.
codex.chapter.ie_start.intro.1: It all starts where real industry started: with coke.
codex.chapter.ie_start.subtitle: Where Immersive Engineering begins
codex.chapter.ie_start.title: Hammer and Coke
codex.chapter.life_furniture.intro.0: The pack has three independent furniture mods plus the decorative blocks of Create, Domum Ornamentum and Eternal Tales. Together they cover any interior.
codex.chapter.life_furniture.subtitle: Handcrafted, Refurbished Furniture, Furnicraft and decor
codex.chapter.life_furniture.title: Furniture and Comfort
codex.chapter.life_world.intro.0: Terralith reshapes the world: real mountain ranges, canyons, cave systems, oases and volcanoes, over a hundred biomes in all.
codex.chapter.life_world.intro.1: Lithostitched and TerraBlender keep it from clashing with the dimensions the other mods add.
codex.chapter.life_world.subtitle: Terralith, compasses and distant rendering
codex.chapter.life_world.title: The Pack's World
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.intro.0: Mystical Agriculture answers the question everyone eventually asks: why dig when you can grow. Diamonds, netherite, a nether star — here they're all seeds.
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.intro.1: The ladder is simple and strict: six essence tiers, each one four of the previous. The higher a crop's tier, the higher the essence its seeds are made from.
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.intro.2: The whole mod is explained by a Patchouli book crafted from a book and a pinch of inferium.
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.subtitle: Six essence tiers and a field instead of a mine
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.title: Mystical Agriculture
codex.chapter.magic_ars.intro.0: Ars Nouveau hands you no finished spells. It hands you building blocks: a form, an effect and augments — and assembling them into something that works is your job.
codex.chapter.magic_ars.intro.1: 'Projectile, break, harm' — and you have a spell that breaks blocks at range. 'Touch, grow, extend time' — an accelerator for your fields. The whole mod rests on that combinatorics.
codex.chapter.magic_ars.intro.2: The resource here is called Source. It collects in jars and travels by relay — through the air, without a single pipe.
codex.chapter.magic_ars.subtitle: Source, glyphs and spells you write yourself
codex.chapter.magic_ars.title: Ars Nouveau
codex.chapter.magic_botania.intro.0: Botania recognises no wires, no interfaces, no numbers on a screen. Flowers decide everything here: some make mana, others spend it, and you arrange them until it adds up to an economy.
codex.chapter.magic_botania.intro.1: Mana is the mod's only resource. It isn't stored in batteries and doesn't flow through pipes: spreaders shoot it through the air, and you have to aim.
codex.chapter.magic_botania.intro.2: Craft the Lexica Botania first. It isn't decoration but a full textbook, and half the mod is explained nowhere else.
codex.chapter.magic_botania.subtitle: Botania: where flower magic begins
codex.chapter.magic_botania.title: Petals and Mana
codex.chapter.magic_botania_end.intro.0: Past terrasteel two doors open. One leads to Alfheim — to elves who won't let you in but trade readily through a portal. The other leads to an arena where the Gaia Guardian waits.
codex.chapter.magic_botania_end.subtitle: Elves, relics and the end of the flower road
codex.chapter.magic_botania_end.title: Alfheim and the Gaia Guardian
Runes are keys. Almost everything interesting Botania does needs a rune of an element, a season or a sin, and they're made only at the Runic Altar.
The good news: catalyst runes come back. One rune of water opens a dozen recipes and stays with you.
codex.chapter.magic_botania_runes.subtit: The second circle: altar, runes, harder flowers
codex.chapter.magic_botania_runes.title: Runes and Terrasteel
codex.chapter.magic_irons.intro.0: If Ars Nouveau is a construction kit, Iron's Spellbooks is about classes. Eight schools: fire, ice, lightning, blood, evocation, ender, holy and nature. Each has its own spells, armor and style.
codex.chapter.magic_irons.intro.1: Spells here are found, not invented: scrolls drop from mobs and lie in chests. Your job is to gather them into a book and tune it to your school.
codex.chapter.magic_irons.subtitle: Eight schools of magic and the battle mage's road
codex.chapter.magic_irons.title: Iron's Spellbooks
codex.chapter.mc_build.subtitle: Structurize, Domum Ornamentum and Multi-Piston
codex.chapter.mc_build.title: Construction and Styles
codex.chapter.mc_found.intro.0: MineColonies is a game where you don't build. You decide what to build, find materials and wait for someone else to lay stone on stone. At first it's annoying. Then it becomes clear the colony grows while you're off in the Twilight Forest, and that's the best kind of automation there is.
codex.chapter.mc_found.subtitle: Town hall, builder and first citizens
codex.chapter.mc_found.title: Founding a Colony
codex.chapter.mc_military.intro.0: Barbarians, pirates, mummies, norsemen, amazons — who comes depends on the biome. How many and how often — on colony size. A late colony without a garrison doesn't live to morning.
codex.chapter.mc_military.subtitle: Guards, barracks and repelling raids
codex.chapter.mc_military.title: Defense
codex.chapter.mc_production.intro.0: The colony can make nearly anything once the chains are set: lumberjack gives logs, sawmill gives products, miner gives ore, smeltery gives ingots, blacksmith gives tools. Your job is deciding what comes first.
codex.chapter.mc_production.subtitle: From forest and mine to smithy and glassblower
codex.chapter.mc_production.title: Colony Production
codex.chapter.mc_research.subtitle: University, school, library and research
codex.chapter.mc_research.title: Science and Growth
codex.chapter.mek_gear.intro.0: MekaSuit by itself is diamond with a battery. Modules decide everything: over thirty, and each turns the suit into something new — a diver, a pilot, a miner who needs no pickaxe.
codex.chapter.mek_gear.subtitle: Power armor, modules and the Meka-Tool
codex.chapter.mek_gear.title: MekaSuit
codex.chapter.mek_nuclear.intro.0: A fission reactor doesn't explode. It melts — slowly, with warning — and leaves land you can't walk on for weeks. That's not punishment for a mistake, it's the price of the pack's strongest source.
codex.chapter.mek_nuclear.intro.1: Build it far away. Set up emergency shutdown before the first fuel load. And don't take the Geiger counter off your belt.
codex.chapter.mek_nuclear.subtitle: Uranium, fission reactor, waste and radiation
codex.chapter.mek_nuclear.title: Nuclear Power
codex.chapter.mek_ore.intro.0: This chapter is why people install Mekanism. Each machine in the chain adds a multiplier: two, three, four, five. Five ingots from one piece of ore isn't convenience — it's a different economy.
codex.chapter.mek_ore.subtitle: From doubling to fivefold yield
codex.chapter.mek_ore.title: Ore Processing
codex.chapter.mek_power.subtitle: From heat generator to steam turbine
codex.chapter.mek_power.title: Power Generation
codex.chapter.mek_qio.subtitle: Quantum storage and instant travel
codex.chapter.mek_qio.title: QIO and Teleportation
codex.chapter.mek_start.intro.0: Mekanism is the strictest of the three tech lines. Four tiers of everything: circuits, alloys, pipes, factories. No part is skipped, but each next one is exactly twice as good.
codex.chapter.mek_start.intro.1: Osmium, infuser, steel, casing. From there the branch unfolds on its own — into chemistry, reactors, armor that flies.
codex.chapter.mek_start.subtitle: Metallurgic infuser, steel and steel casing
codex.chapter.mek_start.title: Osmium and First Machines
codex.chapter.missiles.intro.0: A small mod that stitches Big Cannons, Aeronautics and Radar together: a missile is a physics object with an engine, fins and a guidance system.
codex.chapter.missiles.subtitle: CBC Aeronautics Missiles: guided rocket weapons
codex.chapter.missiles.title: Missiles
codex.chapter.more_et_side.subtitle: What in Eternal Tales doesn't lead to Unahzaal but is worth the time
codex.chapter.more_et_side.title: Side Paths
codex.chapter.more_explore.intro.0: Terralith reshaped the world, and most of it you'll never see unless you go on purpose. This atlas is a list of places worth going. The book marks a biome as soon as you stand in it.
codex.chapter.more_explore.subtitle: Biomes of Terralith and other worlds
codex.chapter.more_explore.title: Atlas
codex.chapter.more_home.subtitle: Comfort as a discipline of its own
codex.chapter.more_home.title: Home
codex.chapter.more_kitchen.subtitle: Farmer's Delight, the MineColonies kitchen and Eternal Tales food
codex.chapter.more_kitchen.title: Cookbook
codex.chapter.more_munitions.subtitle: Munitions, fuzes and battery supply
codex.chapter.more_munitions.title: Arsenal
codex.chapter.more_qol2.intro.0: The pack doubled in size, and the number of small things that make it bearable doubled with it. This chapter is about those.
codex.chapter.more_qol2.subtitle: Gadgets, hammers, bins and everything else that saves hours
codex.chapter.more_qol2.title: New Conveniences
codex.chapter.more_rails.subtitle: Steam 'n' Rails in all its glory
codex.chapter.more_rails.title: Depot
codex.chapter.more_vanilla.intro.0: Under ninety mods lies the same game: diamonds deep down, an enchanting table, netherite, a beacon. Mods don't cancel it — they make it faster and prettier.
codex.chapter.more_vanilla.subtitle: Vanilla progression the pack won't let you forget
codex.chapter.more_vanilla.title: Old Roads
codex.chapter.offroad.subtitle: Wheels, suspension and all-terrain
codex.chapter.offroad.title: Create Offroad: Ground Vehicles
codex.chapter.radar.intro.0: Create Radar links artillery to electronics: radars find targets, controllers aim guns, IFF tells friend from foe.
codex.chapter.radar.subtitle: Detection, air defense and automatic aiming
codex.chapter.radar.title: Create Radar: Targeting
codex.chapter.rs_autocraft.intro.0: Autocrafting is the moment the network stops being a warehouse and becomes a conversation partner. You ask for 'a hundred precision mechanisms', it computes a tree of forty recipes, finds what's missing, and makes it. You wait.
codex.chapter.rs_autocraft.subtitle: Patterns, autocrafters and production chains
codex.chapter.rs_autocraft.title: Refined Storage: Autocrafting
codex.chapter.rs_network.intro.0: Refined Storage moves a warehouse from space into data. Chests, racks, Create vaults — all become lines in one list, and search replaces running between boxes.
codex.chapter.rs_network.intro.1: The network's real value shows later, when it starts doing things itself. But it all begins with a controller and one thousand-item disk.
codex.chapter.rs_network.subtitle: Controller, cables, disks and grids
codex.chapter.rs_network.title: Refined Storage: Network
codex.chapter.space_glacio.intro.0: Another star, another system. Glacio is the only Ad Astra world besides Earth with oxygen: minus twenty, snow, ice peaks and peaceful glacian rams.
codex.chapter.space_glacio.intro.1: The mod's progression ends here. Beyond it is what you build yourself.
codex.chapter.space_glacio.subtitle: Glacio — the end of the road and the start of a colony
codex.chapter.space_glacio.title: Proxima Centauri
codex.chapter.space_ground.intro.0: Space in this pack starts not with stars but with a coal generator and a compressor. Ad Astra asks for exactly what real spaceflight asked for: metal, electricity and a great deal of patience.
codex.chapter.space_ground.intro.1: The path is single and strict: steel, plates, NASA workbench, rocket. Oxygen and fuel come separately, and without them a rocket is a monument.
codex.chapter.space_ground.intro.2: The mod's in-game guide is called Astrodux. Craft it first: same steps, but with pictures.
codex.chapter.space_ground.subtitle: Steel, oxygen, fuel and the first rocket
codex.chapter.space_ground.title: Launch Table
codex.chapter.space_hot.intro.0: Four hundred sixty-four degrees, acid rain and leaden clouds. Venus is the most hostile place in the pack, and calorite lies exactly there.
codex.chapter.space_hot.intro.1: Mercury is simpler: a hundred sixty-seven degrees, not a drop of water and the brightest sun in the system — panels work there like nowhere else.
codex.chapter.space_hot.subtitle: Venus, Mercury and calorite
codex.chapter.space_hot.title: The Hot Planets
codex.chapter.space_mars.intro.0: Red dust, minus sixty-five and canyons deeper than Earth's. Mars holds ostrum — the metal you make things from that survive Venus.
codex.chapter.space_mars.subtitle: Ostrum, cryo fuel and a real colony
codex.chapter.space_mars.title: Mars
codex.chapter.space_moon.intro.0: Grey wasteland to the horizon, black sky and gravity six times weaker than home. There's nothing to breathe, water freezes in mid-air and torches go out — and here lies desh, without which you fly no further.
codex.chapter.space_moon.subtitle: First step, desh and life under a dome
codex.chapter.space_moon.title: The Moon
codex.chapter.start_first_day.intro.0: The first sunrise in this pack looks like any other: the same oaks, the same creak of a crafting table. The difference shows by evening, when it turns out nine foreign worlds, three industrial civilizations and a colony that grows without you are all waiting.
codex.chapter.start_first_day.intro.1: This chapter is about the first hours. Not how to survive, but how not to owe your future self: don't build where you'll have to move from, and don't spend a day on what a mod does in a second.
codex.chapter.start_first_day.subtitle: Where the pack begins and what not to rush into
codex.chapter.start_first_day.title: First Day
codex.chapter.start_qol.intro.0: This chapter is a reference. Nothing here is mandatory, but every entry is worth reading: half the small annoyances of vanilla are already solved here, and it's a shame to learn that at hour one hundred.
codex.chapter.start_qol.subtitle: Mods that add nothing to progression but change everything
codex.chapter.start_qol.title: Pack Conveniences
codex.chapter.storage_local.subtitle: Backpacks, chests and everything that needs no network
codex.chapter.storage_local.title: Local Storage
codex.chapter.story_colony.intro.0: MineColonies is the only mod in the pack where progress happens while you're away. This line is about how a supply chest grows into a city that supplies your factory, and the factory supplies it.
codex.chapter.story_colony.subtitle: The colony from four citizens to a technopolis
codex.chapter.story_colony.title: A City That Grows Itself
codex.chapter.story_current.intro.0: The pack's three technologies live apart for a long time: Create spins shafts, IE strings wires, Mekanism keeps quiet and enriches. This line is about making them talk to each other, and it ends with a reactor that feeds everything.
codex.chapter.story_current.subtitle: Three factories — one power grid
codex.chapter.story_current.title: Current
codex.chapter.story_expedition.intro.0: The pack leads you through foreign worlds not at random but in order: sky first, then twilight, then comets — and onward along the spiral Volcanech's war laid out. This line is a route, and it has only one destination.
codex.chapter.story_expedition.subtitle: Through every world, in the order they open
codex.chapter.story_expedition.title: Expedition
codex.chapter.story_forge.intro.0: There's an easy way to know what your factory is worth: stop walking up to it. This line leads from a hand on a crank to a train that leaves for the mine on schedule and returns with ore while you sleep.
codex.chapter.story_forge.intro.1: The forks are real: you can go through wind or water, through millstone or wheels. They meet on one thing — the train.
codex.chapter.story_forge.subtitle: From the first alloy to a train that hauls ore by itself
codex.chapter.story_forge.title: The Engineer's Road
codex.chapter.story_sky.intro.0: An airship without a gun is a stroll. A gun without radar is fireworks. This line gathers three mods into one system: flying platform, targeting, salvo.
codex.chapter.story_sky.subtitle: Air fleet, artillery and radar — one defense
codex.chapter.story_sky.title: Sky and Powder
codex.chapter.tech2_foregoing.intro.0: Industrial Foregoing is a set of machines with no single chain: each does one job and does it well. Plants, harvests, milks, shears, kills, smelts, stores.
codex.chapter.tech2_foregoing.intro.1: It starts with latex tapped out of logs and ends with a laser that fires into bedrock and pulls ore back out without a single pickaxe.
codex.chapter.tech2_foregoing.subtitle: Latex, lasers and farms that run themselves
codex.chapter.tech2_foregoing.title: Industrial Foregoing
codex.chapter.tech2_mektools.intro.0: Mekanism Tools takes the main mod's metals and makes a full set of tools, armor, shields and paxels from them.
codex.chapter.tech2_mektools.intro.1: The point isn't variety but numbers: two materials here are honestly better than netherite, and one is the fastest tool in the game.
codex.chapter.tech2_mektools.subtitle: Six materials that beat netherite
codex.chapter.tech2_mektools.title: Mekanism Tools
codex.chapter.tech2_newage.intro.0: Create Addition gives you simple generators. Create: New Age goes further — magnets, coils, motors and a real nuclear reactor that melts down if you forget the cooling.
codex.chapter.tech2_newage.intro.1: Both branches run on the same energy, so there's no choosing: take whatever suits from each.
codex.chapter.tech2_newage.subtitle: Electricity, heat and a nuclear reactor for Create
codex.chapter.tech2_newage.title: Create: New Age
codex.chapter.tech2_petroleum.intro.0: An Immersive Engineering addon that gives it an oil industry: survey, drilling, extraction and refining.
codex.chapter.tech2_petroleum.intro.1: Oil sits in reservoirs under whole regions. Finding one is half the job; the other half is building a pumpjack over it.
codex.chapter.tech2_petroleum.subtitle: Oil, wells and what's distilled from them
codex.chapter.tech2_petroleum.title: Immersive Petroleum
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.intro.0: PneumaticCraft is the only mod in the pack where a machine can explode simply because you pumped too much air into it. Pressure is a real resource here: scarce, slow to build and instant to lose.
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.intro.1: At the end of the road stand drones — small robots you draw a program for out of instruction blocks and send off to dig, build, harvest or fight.
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.intro.2: It all starts with compressed iron: you put iron ingots in a fire and blow them up.
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.subtitle: Pressure, plastic and drones you program yourself
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.title: PneumaticCraft
codex.chapter.tech2_powah.intro.0: Powah invents no mechanics — it delivers energy simply and reliably. Five kinds of generator, cells of any size, cables and wireless transfer.
codex.chapter.tech2_powah.intro.1: Everything comes in five tiers: starter, basic, hardened, blazing, niotic, spirited and nitro. Only the numbers change, but they change fast.
codex.chapter.tech2_powah.subtitle: Energy without complications: generators, cells, reactor
codex.chapter.tech2_powah.title: Powah
codex.chapter.trials_bosses.intro.0: Nothing to turn in here: the book sees the advancement itself and pays. But the rewards here are the biggest.
codex.chapter.trials_bosses.subtitle: Boss victories the book can notice
codex.chapter.trials_bosses.title: Trials: Trophies
codex.chapter.trials_early.intro.0: Trials work differently from the other chapters. Here the book doesn't ask to see an item — it takes it: press 'Turn in', and the items vanish from your inventory in exchange for a reward.
codex.chapter.trials_early.intro.1: Rewards are chosen to be worth more than what you gave — but only if you came for them in time.
codex.chapter.trials_early.intro.2: Without the mod on the server, items aren't taken and no reward is given: the trial just gets checked off.
codex.chapter.trials_early.subtitle: Turn in resources — get what speeds the start
codex.chapter.trials_early.title: Trials: First Days
codex.chapter.trials_late.intro.0: Here what you give is truly costly. Rewards are items that don't exist in the world: speed modules, disks, top-tier circuits.
codex.chapter.trials_late.subtitle: Turning in rare materials at the pack's peak
codex.chapter.trials_late.title: Trials: High Technology
codex.chapter.trials_mid.intro.0: Once production runs, turning in a stack of product is easy. Rewards here are parts whose cost isn't material but assembly time.
codex.chapter.trials_mid.subtitle: Machine output in exchange for machines
codex.chapter.trials_mid.title: Trials: Factory Hum
codex.msg.not_enough: Codex: not enough items to turn in
codex.quest.aero_basics.airship.text.0: Gondola, envelope on top, burner, a steam vent for dumping, assembler. The first ascent is always crooked; the first flight over your own base is always silent.
codex.quest.aero_basics.airship.title: First Airship
codex.quest.aero_basics.assembler.text.0: A click — and the build stops being part of the world. It gains mass, inertia and the ability to fall. Disassembled with the same block.
codex.quest.aero_basics.assembler.title: Physics Assembler
codex.quest.aero_basics.burner_aero.text: Heats the air in the envelope. Hotter fire — higher. A signal is the regulator.
codex.quest.aero_basics.docking.text.0: A connector joins two vessels, a paired one is a hinge. Ropes tow and moor. An airship port — reality.
codex.quest.aero_basics.docking.title: Docking and Mooring
codex.quest.aero_basics.engine.text.0: Rotation aboard, without a boiler or shafts from the ground.
codex.quest.aero_basics.engine.title: Portable Engine
codex.quest.aero_basics.envelope.text.0: A balloon. Its volume is the lift. An envelope with a shaft inside passes rotation through itself. Sixteen colors.
codex.quest.aero_basics.envelope.title: Airship Envelope
codex.quest.aero_basics.goggles_aero.tex: Altitude, speed, roll, pitch — on the glass.
codex.quest.aero_basics.gyro.text.0: Without a gyroscope the ship lists and one day flips. With one it stands in the air as if on a table.
codex.quest.aero_basics.gyro.title: Gyroscopes
codex.quest.aero_basics.levitite.text.0: A material with negative mass. The blend brews in a basin from ender powder, is poured and sets into blocks that pull upward. Pearlescent — for heavy vessels.
codex.quest.aero_basics.levitite.title: Levitite
Map, route, a typewriter with a program and a receiver. A ship that flies itself while you sleep in its hold.
codex.quest.aero_basics.navigation.title: Navigation Table
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.text.0: Wooden light, andesite tough, smart changes pitch in flight. On a propeller bearing, on a shaft, forward.
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.title: Propellers
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.text.0: Altimeter, gimbal, optics, laser. Autopilot is assembled from these: the altimeter holds level, the gimbal evens the wings.
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.title: Sensors
codex.quest.ca_electric.accumulator.text: Stores. The modular one grows into a battery of any size.
A shaft goes in — energy comes out. Faster shaft, more energy and more stress. Water wheel, controller, alternator: the pack's first power plant fits on a table.
codex.quest.ca_electric.alternator.title: Alternator
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.text.0: A retired blaze: a burner on bioethanol or oil heats a basin just as well. Biomass from plants, pellets under the press, distillation — and fuel grows in the garden.
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.title: Liquid Blaze Burner
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.text.0: A connector on the machine, a cable between connectors. Large carries more current, the light one powers lamps, the relay breaks the circuit on a signal.
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.title: Connectors and Cables
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.text.0: Reads a Create machine and speaks in numbers: level, speed, presence.
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.title: Digital Adapter
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.text.0: Gold with zinc in the mixer. The mod's best conductor and the material of an amulet that stores experience.
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.title: Electrum
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.text.0: The reverse translation: energy into rotation at a set speed. A motor in a locomotive instead of a boiler — and the train charges at the station like a phone.
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.title: Electric Motor
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.text.0: Energy between a contraption and the grid. The train pulls up — charges — leaves.
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.title: Portable Energy Interface
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.text.0: Ingot to rod, rod to wire. No wire, no spools; no spools, no cables.
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.title: Rolling Mill
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.text.0: Lightning at everything alive nearby. Also charges items and turns sand to glass on a belt. Don't put it by the entrance.
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.title: Tesla Coil
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.text.0: Copper conducts, gold better, electrum best of all. Wire on a spool becomes a cable strung between connectors.
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.title: Wire and Spools
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.text.0: The armor inspection tool shows which block takes which charge. The gas mask protects from gas shells.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.text.1: Planning a fortification, check blocks with this tool — intuition lies here.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.title: Armor and Protection
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.text.0: AP, incendiary and flak rounds solve different problems. A tracer tip helps correct fire.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.title: Autocannon Rounds
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autocannon.text: The autocannon fires bursts of unitary cartridges. Needs a barrel, a breech with extractor and a recoil spring.
Cartridges are assembled from cases, powder and rounds; the ammo container feeds the belt.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.text.0: A muzzle-loader needs cleaning after every shot. The sliding breech loads from the rear, the quick-firing one uses cartridges.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.title: Breeches
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.text.0: Bronze barrels take a bigger charge than cast iron and wear slower.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.title: Bronze
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.text.0: Lobs at short range. Cheap and effective against fortifications.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.title: Mortar
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.nethersteel.tex: Top of the line. Nethersteel barrels and screw breeches fire the heaviest charges without risk of bursting.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.text.0: HE explodes, AP pierces, shrapnel covers infantry, smoke screens, fluid spills a tank's contents.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.text.1: Each shell takes a fuze: impact, inertia, timed, proximity or wired.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.title: Shells
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.text.0: Steel guns are the mod's workhorse. Built-up barrels appear — several layers — taking maximum charges.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.title: Steel
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.text.0: Cast iron is the cheapest. It takes only weak charges, but enough to learn the mechanics.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.text.1: A barrel is assembled from sections: the chamber, several barrel sections and the end.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.title: First Barrel
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.text.0: A mold is assembled from sections of different diameter (very small through very large). Pour melt, wait for it to set — a finished cast.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.text.1: The sections set the future gun's caliber.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.title: Barrel Mold
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.text.0: An unbored casting can't fire: it must be bored on a drilling rig. The rig is a contraption with a drill bit that travels along the barrel.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.text.1: Only after boring is the barrel usable.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.title: Boring
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.text.0: The cannon loader with a ram rod and worm automates the cycle: extract, clean, load, fire.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.text.1: A battery with autoloading fires continuously.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.title: Autoloading
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.text.0: Metal melts in a Create basin under a foundry lid on high heat. Cast iron from iron and coal, bronze from copper and zinc, steel from iron with additives.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.text.1: Melt is stored in ordinary Create tanks and poured with a spout.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.title: Melting Metal
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.text.0: The cannon mount aims horizontally and vertically, driven by Create controls or a targeting controller.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.text.1: The fixed mount is cheaper but doesn't turn; the wheeled carriage is hauled by hand.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.title: Mount and Carriage
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.text.0: A charge is pressed powder in a casing. Charge count sets range and damage, but exceeding the barrel's limit bursts it.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.text.1: Guncotton and nitropowder are stronger than plain powder.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.title: Powder Charge
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.text.0: Foundry sand is the consumable for molds. Sand and clay.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.title: Casting Sand
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.text.0: Loading order: charge, then projectile, then ignition (flint or redstone at the chamber).
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.text.1: Solid shot pierces, grapeshot sprays, a stone ball is the cheapest.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.title: First Shot
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.text.0: The welder joins sections into one gun. Without welding the shot tears the seam.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.title: Welding Sections
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.text.0: Two shafts and a connector between them — a belt appears. Items ride it, creatures ride it, you ride it; press and saw work above it. Up to twenty blocks, no steeper than forty-five degrees.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.text.1: With belts, Create stops being a set of tools and becomes a line.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.title: Mechanical Belts
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.text.0: For the basin to heat, fire must live under it — not any fire, a blaze. Take an empty burner to the Nether and catch the spirit with a click. Feed it coal for normal heat and blaze cake for white flame: each has its own recipes.
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.title: Blaze Burner
Alloy and planks. A casing is a shell for a mechanism; at first made by hand, later stamped by the hundred.
codex.quest.create_andesite.casing.title: Andesite Casing
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.text.0: Vertical. A plain chute drops down; a smart one filters and, given rotation, pulls up.
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.title: Chutes
codex.quest.create_andesite.crafter_basi: A crafting table taken apart into cells. Each is a block; the wrench sets where cells pass contents, and at the end an item assembles. The only way to make precision mechanisms not one at a time but by the hundred.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.text.0: A depot is a one-item table: the press strikes over it, the saw cuts, the deployer works. A funnel puts in and takes out. The brass one can also choose.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.title: Depot and Funnels
codex.quest.create_andesite.ejector.text: Flings an item or creature to a set point. Configured with the wrench. A catapult lift is an old and working joke.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.text.0: The fan pushes air. Through fire — it smelts. Through water — washes. Through lava — smokes. Through ice — freezes. The cheapest ore processing in the mod: a stream of crushed iron through a fan over fire, and ingots rain onto the belt.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.title: Encased Fan
codex.quest.create_andesite.millstone.re: Ore doubling at the early stage
codex.quest.create_andesite.millstone.te: Slow, modest, honest. Takes rotation only from above, grinds one item at a time and barely loads the network. But raw iron in it becomes crushed ore, and crushed ore smelts to one and a half ingots. The first ore doubling.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.text.0: A mixer over a basin is already alchemy. Andesite alloy by the batch, brass, chocolate, concrete, dough: anything that needs 'mixing' happens here. The basin ejects the result itself if a depot stands below.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.title: Mechanical Mixer
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.text.0: The first machine that does something hands can't. An ingot becomes a sheet, a stack of planks a casing. The press strikes what's under it: a depot or a belt running below.
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.text.1: Sheets are the consumable of everything to come. Iron, copper, gold, brass.
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.title: Mechanical Press
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.text.0: A horizontal saw cuts what rides the belt: planks, shafts, slabs. Vertical, it fells trees and — given rotation and room — becomes a sawmill that works while you sleep.
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.title: Mechanical Saw
It all starts with the ugliest stone in the game. Andesite with an iron or zinc nugget pressed to it becomes alloy — dull, gray and irreplaceable. Shafts, cogs, casings and half of what you'll build in the coming days come from it.
Zinc is found in mountains and caves: raw zinc smelts to an ingot, the ingot goes into brass. Iron will do for now.
codex.quest.create_basics.andesite.title: Andesite Alloy
Three by three, one item, noticeably stronger. Of the early sources it's the most honest: no coal, no attention, no surprises.
codex.quest.create_basics.bigwheel.title: Large Water Wheel
Two cogs side by side spin opposite ways. A small one meshed with a large one halves the speed and doubles available stress; the reverse speeds up and drains. Create's entire gearbox fits in that rule.
Two small cogs flush together jam the network. It's the first thing everyone breaks.
codex.quest.create_basics.cogwheel.title: Cogwheels
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.text.0: In the helmet slot. Speed, stress, tank contents — right in the block tooltip, no gauges.
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.title: Engineer's Goggles
codex.quest.create_basics.handcrank.text: A handle you can turn. While you hold it, the mechanism lives. Gates, a lift, a single press at the start — your arms won't manage more, and more isn't needed yet.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.task.0: Open the Ponder scene for a cogwheel (W key)
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.text.0: Every Create block has a tiny theater. Hover over an item, hold W — and the mechanism is assembled and started before your eyes, with commentary. It's the mod's best documentation, and the book sees when you watch.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.title: Ponder Scenes
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.text.0: A frame covered in wool counts as a full sail. Fewer blocks — same thrust.
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.title: Sails
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.text.0: A shaft does nothing. It passes things on: speed as is, direction as is, stress into the network's common pot. Everything else is built from such 'nothings'.
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.text.1: Later a saw will cut shafts: six per alloy.
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.title: Shaft
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.text.0: Two needles without which Create is guesswork. The stressometer shows how much the network pulls and how much it can; the speedometer, how fast. Needle in the red — add a source or drop speed with cogs.
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.title: Stressometer and Speedometer
codex.quest.create_basics.waterwheel.tex: The first source that never tires. Eight RPM, a modest stress budget, but forever. Put it in a real flowing current — better yet a closed channel with sources — and the paddles catch water from every side.
A windmill bearing and sails around it. More area, more force; the cap is 128 sail blocks. Build the wings right on the bearing, click — and the structure tears free of the world and goes round.
It's the first contraption of your life. There will be many.
codex.quest.create_basics.windmill.title: Windmill
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.text.0: Rotates, picks up with settings kept, gives hints. You won't put the wrench down until the very end — make two.
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.title: Wrench
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.text.0: The wrench marks where to take from and where to put — and the arm carries, filtering at each point. One manipulator instead of a dozen funnels.
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.title: Mechanical Arm
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.text.0: Copper and zinc in a hot basin. Normal heat is enough. Everything that can think is made of this yellow metal.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.title: Brass
codex.quest.create_brass.brass_casing.te: The base of filtering funnels, logic tunnels and machines that decide for themselves.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass_funnel.te: The funnel picks by item, the tunnel splits a stream evenly, in turn or by filter. The attribute filter understands words like 'food', 'tool', 'enchanted' — and sorts by meaning.
Chromatic compound under light — Refined Radiance; in the dark under pressure — Shadow Steel. Materials for top-tier casings and for those who like pretty things.
codex.quest.create_brass.chromatic.title: Chromatics
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.text.0: Two wheels turning toward each other. Everything that falls between is ground — ore, stone, a careless player. Unlike the millstone, the wheels eat a stream, and that's the main ore doubling for the whole mid-game.
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.title: Crushing Wheels
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.text.0: A mechanical hand with one gesture: click, hit, plant, milk. On a contraption — the heart of any farm; on a line — an assembler that never gets bored.
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.title: Deployer
Gold sheet, rods, cogs — and five crafters in a ring with deployers. The mechanism only assembles on a line, and it's the first thing in Create you can't make without Create. From here on everything needs it: schedules, radars, late automation.
codex.quest.create_brass.precision.title: Precision Mechanism
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.text.0: A cube of blocks — one inventory for all: funnels, arms, packagers and, later, the Refined Storage network.
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.title: Item Vault
Spins a structure around itself. Carousel, swing bridge, windmill, circular assembly line.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.cart.tex: The assembler turns a build over a rail into a riding minecart. Coupling makes two carts a train long before real trains.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.clockwor: One turn per day. A tower clock, a shadow crawling across the square — pure decoration, and no less lovely for it.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.controls: The controls switch parts of the machine from inside. The seat sits you down, the train controls give you a train. A machine you ride is a different kind of relationship.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.elevator: A real elevator: a contact on each floor, a sign with the name, a button. You wait for the car — and it comes.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.gantry.t: A carriage rides a shaft-rail and drags anything behind it. Chunk-sized quarries start here.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.glue.tex: Glue binds blocks into a group. A linear chassis pulls along an axis, a radial one in a circle; range set with the wrench.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.piston.t: Moves in a straight line the length of the poles. Sticky brings it back. Gates, bridges, sliding walls.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.pulley.t: Lowers and raises. A mine lift, a rig lowered into the abyss.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.tools_co: The drill breaks, the saw fells, the plough tills and collects, the harvester reaps, the roller lays road. All of it works only in motion — and in motion never tires.
The backtank stores compressed air while a shaft spins it, and hands it to a helmet underwater. Netherite holds more and doesn't fear lava.
codex.quest.create_copper.backtank.title: Copper Backtank
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.text.0: A tank of water, burners beneath, engines on the sides. A boiler has a level — one to eighteen — growing with volume, burner count and fire quality. Each engine takes its share and spins a shaft. Nothing in the mod gives this much force from so small a footprint.
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.title: Steam Boiler
Copper sheets and planks. Needed for encased pipes, the hose pulley and all steam tech.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.text.0: The helmet breathes from the tank, the boots hold you on the bottom. The ocean stops being a wall.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.title: Diving Gear
codex.quest.create_copper.netherite_divi: In it you walk the floor of Nether lava lakes. Slowly, but you walk.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.text.0: Pitch set with extensions. Melodies are built from whistles — and the train horn heard beyond the hill.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.title: Steam Whistle
codex.quest.create_fluids.chocolate.text: Cocoa in a hot basin — chocolate. Honeycomb — honey. Not just food: honey goes into recipes, and chocolate berries are more filling than they look.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.text.0: The hose drops into a lake and drinks it to the bottom. Or the reverse — fills it. A large enough body counts as infinite, and then it's an eternal source.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.title: Hose Pulley
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.text.0: Glass ones show what's inside. Smart ones filter. A valve shuts on a signal. Plain ones just connect the ends.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.title: Fluid Pipes
codex.quest.create_fluids.portable_fluid: The contraption pulls up, interfaces dock — and fluid and items flow into the fixed network. That's how trains and drilling rigs unload.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.text.0: The pump gives fluid direction and speed. Without it the network is a drawing. Direction changes with a wrench or a signal.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.title: Mechanical Pump
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.text.0: The spout pours onto an item — that's how blaze cakes are made and bottles filled. The drain pulls back out of buckets.
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.title: Spout and Drain
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.text.0: Tanks merge into a reservoir of any size; the window shows the level. Taller means more.
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.title: Fluid Tank
codex.quest.create_kinetics.chaindrive.t: A row of shafts linked by chain spins as one. The adjustable drive doubles speed on the whole row on a signal.
The clutch breaks transmission on a signal, the gearshift reverses it. 'Gearshift plus pulse' is the standard way to make a piston go back and forth.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.clutch.title: Clutch and Gearshift
codex.quest.create_kinetics.display.text: The display link reads a machine and writes to a sign, board or nixie tubes. Counters, levels, departure boards — all of them.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.flywheel.tex: A tank of water, burners beneath, engine on the side, flywheel at the output. The mid-game power plant looks exactly like this and hums accordingly.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.gearbox.text: Four sides, two directions. The vertical gearbox does the same along Y. Without it a shaft can't turn a corner.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.text.0: Two items set a frequency, and the signal flies through air. The linked controller is a remote with buttons on chosen frequencies: a machine you run from another room.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.title: Wireless Link
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.text.0: Repeater, pulse extender, timer, latch, analog lever, contact. All the automation — without kilometers of dust.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.title: Redstone Logic
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.text.0: Sits under a large cog and tells it an exact speed, −256 to 256. Needs brass and settles most arguments with gearing for good.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.title: Rotation Speed Controller
codex.quest.create_kinetics.sequenced.te: A program of steps: turn this much, wait, reverse. Doors, lifts, assembly carousels — all on it.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.stockpile.te: The stockpile switch watches fullness, the content observer watches presence, the track observer watches for trains. Three ways to ask the world what it thinks.
codex.quest.create_packages.cardboard.te: Paper under the press. From cardboard — packages, package filters and armor mobs don't notice you in. The last part isn't a joke.
codex.quest.create_packages.chain_convey: A chain between nodes over any distance. Boxes ride it — and you, if you grab on. The cheapest way to link distant builds.
codex.quest.create_packages.factory_gaug: The gauge knows what should lie at the output and how much. If it's short, it orders the missing from neighboring gauges, and they from theirs. A factory built on gauges doesn't wait for commands: it plans.
codex.quest.create_packages.frogport.tex: A frog on a chain. Catches packages, sends packages, unloads into a chest. It croaks if you listen.
codex.quest.create_packages.packager.tex: Takes from an inventory, puts in a box, writes the address. On order or on request. The repackager later reassembles contents.
codex.quest.create_packages.postbox.text: The address is written on the package. A box with that address accepts it — wherever it stands.
codex.quest.create_packages.requester.te: A signal — and the stock sends a set. A machine that orders its own raw materials.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.text.0: Table cloth, bell, ticker — and it's a store. On servers, markets grow from these.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.title: Shop
codex.quest.create_packages.stock_link.t: Hangs on a storage and reports to the ticker what's inside.
The whole stock in one window. Ordered — packagers packed, frogs delivered. The shopping list remembers what you order every time.
codex.quest.create_packages.ticker.title: Stock Ticker
A recipe on the wall. Click — assembled from your inventory.
codex.quest.create_tools.blueprint.title: Crafting Blueprint
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.text.0: The cannon fires blocks from a chest by blueprint — and on empty ground rises a building you built once somewhere else. Gunpowder as fuel adds gravity to the affair.
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.title: Schematicannon
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.text.0: Your arms get longer. Two grips — longer still.
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.title: Extendo Grip
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.text.0: Shoots what grows. Potatoes hit, beetroot stains, fire noodles burn. With a backtank — in bursts.
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.title: Potato Cannon
The quill outlines an area and saves it to a file. The table loads the file into an empty schematic. A building becomes an item.
codex.quest.create_tools.schematic.title: Schematics
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.text.0: Place a block on the left — it appears on the right. Symmetrical buildings in half the time.
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.title: Wand of Symmetry
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.text.0: Eight item sets handed to the hotbar by hotkey to everyone nearby.
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.title: Toolbox
codex.quest.create_tools.worldshaper.tex: A creative terrain tool. Not in survival; worth knowing about.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.text.0: Train, direction, arrival time. Passengers like it.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.title: Board
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.text.0: Small for wagons, large for the locomotive. Steam 'n' Rails adds double-axle and narrow-gauge.
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.title: Bogeys
codex.quest.create_trains.railway_casing: Stations, signals, bogeys, controls. Everything railway starts with it.
Go there, wait for loading, wait a minute, go back. Conditions — inventory, signal, time of day. Hand the schedule to a conductor — and the train stops needing you.
codex.quest.create_trains.schedule.title: Schedule
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.text.0: A signal divides the track into blocks and keeps a second train out of an occupied one. On a single-track line with opposing traffic, without them there'll be a catastrophe — a beautiful one, but a catastrophe.
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.title: Signals
A cap on a villager — and he drives the train by schedule. The whistle calls the train to the nearest station, like a taxi.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_coupler.te: Screw, knuckle, link-and-pin. Trains uncouple on the move, buffers absorb the bump, headstocks make wagon ends look like wagon ends.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_handcar.te: Pump the lever — you go. No boiler, no schedule, no dignity.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_style.text: Smokestacks, boilers, smokeboxes, locometal in every color, hazard stripes, paint in pitchers. None of it is needed. All of it is wanted.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.text.0: Here the train is assembled and here it stops. Bogeys on the track, body on top, the 'Assemble' button — and the train exists.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.title: Station
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.text.0: Obsidian through press and millstone. Material for what must bear a train's weight.
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.title: Sturdy Sheet
codex.quest.create_trains.track.text.0: Two points — and Create lays the curve, climb or loop between them. Tracks can run through air; supports grow on their own. Thirty-two for the first line to the mine.
codex.quest.create_trains.track.title: Tracks
codex.quest.create_trains.train.text.0: A locomotive needs power aboard: a boiler with an engine or, later, an electric motor. Controls are yours, the seat is the driver's. The first time the train moves with you inside, you'll understand what all this was for.
codex.quest.create_trains.train.title: First Train
codex.quest.create_world.arise.task.0: Find a Create structure in the world
codex.quest.create_world.arise.text.0: Abandoned factories, workshops, mines with working mechanisms. Someone built here before you — and left, leaving blueprints in chests.
codex.quest.create_world.arise.title: Create: Structures Arise
codex.quest.create_world.deco.text.0: Copper shingles in every stage of green, framed glass, girders, brackets, copycat blocks that take any look. Create knows how to be beautiful.
codex.quest.create_world.deco.title: Decorative Blocks
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.text.0: Mills, sawmills, farmyards. Village Create, fitted into Terralith's hills.
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.title: Create: Rustic Structures
codex.quest.create_world.stickywheels.te: Sticky tires for Offroad: hold a slope, don't slip on ice.
Rings, pendants, capes, gloves. The ice pendant freezes water underfoot, the golden feather slows falls, the cloak hides.
codex.quest.dim_aether.accessories.title: Accessories
codex.quest.dim_aether.aether_portal.tex: A frame of glowstone, a bucket of water instead of fire. Islands above, below a void that throws you back to the overworld. Bring something for a soft landing.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.text.0: Enchants on ambrosium and turns gravitite enchanted. The freezer beside it makes ice and icestone.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.title: Altar
codex.quest.dim_aether.bronze_dungeon.te: The Slider: a stone cube that charges and rams. Hit the eye when it pauses.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gold_dungeon.text: The Sun Spirit burns, and while it burns it's invulnerable. Snowballs. Many snowballs. Then — the Hammer of Kingbdogz and phoenix armor.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.text.0: Armor you leap over a house in, and tools that lift blocks into the air. The sky's best material.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.title: Gravitite
codex.quest.dim_aether.holystone.text.0: Skyroot, holystone, ambrosium. An ambrosium shard is both fuel and medicine.
codex.quest.dim_aether.holystone.title: First Tools
codex.quest.dim_aether.lore.text.0: Place an item — and the book tells of it.
codex.quest.dim_aether.lore.title: Book of Lore
codex.quest.dim_aether.moa.text.0: Egg in the incubator, chick fed with petals. A grown moa jumps in the air several times in a row: blue three, white four, black eight.
codex.quest.dim_aether.moa.title: Moa
codex.quest.dim_aether.silver_dungeon.te: Valkyries don't hand over the lance. Take it by force — and the Queen comes out herself.
codex.quest.dim_aether.zanite.text.0: Local iron that speeds up as it wears.
codex.quest.dim_aether.zanite.title: Zanite
codex.quest.dim_end.dragon.text.0: After it — islands, elytra, breath in bottles and an egg several recipes ask for.
codex.quest.dim_end.dragon.title: Ender Dragon
codex.quest.dim_end.elytra.text.0: The best transport until the gravitational modulator.
codex.quest.dim_end.elytra.title: Elytra
codex.quest.dim_end.end_et.text.0: Somewhere in the End stands a portal to Eden. A sunstone from Purgatorium opens it — but that's an Eternal Tales story.
codex.quest.dim_end.end_et.title: Gates of the Gardens of Eden
codex.quest.dim_end.shulker.text.0: Boxes and a few mod recipes.
codex.quest.dim_end.shulker.title: Shulkers
codex.quest.dim_end.stronghold.text.0: Eyes of ender lead to the portal. Pearls will be wanted later too: by levitite and teleporters.
codex.quest.dim_end.stronghold.title: Stronghold
codex.quest.dim_nether.ancient.text.0: Diving set, nethersteel for cannons, top tools. Dig at fifteen.
codex.quest.dim_nether.ancient.title: Netherite
codex.quest.dim_nether.blaze.text.0: Rods — for Create, potions and Eternal Tales rituals. An empty burner catches the spirit itself: walk up to a blaze and click. It doesn't mind.
codex.quest.dim_nether.blaze.title: Blazes
codex.quest.dim_nether.fortress.text.0: Fortress — blazes and wart. Bastion — gold and scrap. Between them — Eternal Tales builds that vanilla never had.
codex.quest.dim_nether.fortress.title: Fortress and Bastion
codex.quest.dim_nether.nether_et.task.0: Find the clocktower in the Nether
codex.quest.dim_nether.nether_et.text.0: A tower with a clock and four locks that piglins didn't build. Keys are with the overseers of the Blazing Wastes. Inside — a trace of Amber and Volcanech.
codex.quest.dim_nether.nether_et.title: Piglin Clocktower
codex.quest.dim_nether.portal.text.0: Obsidian, flint and steel, a step. A supply chest with Carry On goes through the portal right in your hands.
codex.quest.dim_nether.portal.title: Portal
codex.quest.dim_nether.quartz.text.0: Silicon for the network, rose quartz for Create, parts for IE. A stack — minimum.
codex.quest.dim_nether.quartz.title: Nether Quartz
codex.quest.dim_twilight.charms.text.0: Of life — resurrects. Of keeping — keeps inventory. Both single-use.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.charms.title: Charms
codex.quest.dim_twilight.cinders.text.0: Burns away the thorns sealing the last lands. Beyond — only forest.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.cinders.title: Lamp of Cinders
codex.quest.dim_twilight.giants.text.0: Uberous soil, magic beans, a stalk to the clouds. Up top — giants and a pickaxe that breaks four by four.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.giants.title: Cloud Castle
codex.quest.dim_twilight.hydra.text.0: Three heads. A severed one regrows unless finished. Blood and tears — into fiery ingot and sword.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.hydra.title: Hydra
Four ghosts in waves in the dark forest stronghold. Knightmetal — from there.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.lich.reward.0: Opens the labyrinth, swamp and dark forest
codex.quest.dim_twilight.lich.text.0: Three phases: shield and orbs, minions, melee. Reflect the orbs — otherwise the shield won't drop.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.lich.title: Lich
codex.quest.dim_twilight.minoshroom.text: Deep in the labyrinth. The mazebreaker pickaxe breaks its walls.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.naga.text.0: A courtyard with columns. She charges and smashes them; hide and strike.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.naga.title: Naga
codex.quest.dim_twilight.snow_queen.text: First the Alpha Yeti and its fur. Then the ice tower. The glass sword strikes once — but how.
A two-by-two pit, water, flowers around, a diamond into the water. Lightning — and eternal evening.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.tf_portal.title: Portal to the Twilight Forest
codex.quest.dim_twilight.tf_start.text.0: Liveroot and ironwood — the first materials. Torchberries glow, the moonworm queen places lights, the magic map shows where to go.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.tf_start.title: First Steps
codex.quest.dim_twilight.trophy.text.0: Trophy on the pedestal — a buff and opened areas.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.trophy.title: Trophy Pedestal
codex.quest.dim_twilight.uncrafting.text: Takes items back apart. In this pack — a weapon; use with care.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.ur_ghast.text.0: Dark tower, ghast traps, carminite. Experiment 115 — food that never runs out.
codex.quest.dim_twilight.ur_ghast.title: Ur-Ghast
A stabilized black hole, the Order of the Universe, the First Prism, both Ultimate items. Everything left by a civilization that could do more than us.
codex.quest.end_apotheosis.arkemer.title: Arkemer Legacy
codex.quest.end_apotheosis.codex.text.0: The three nodes above — and one nether star in hand. The book has nothing more to tell you. Thank you for reading to the end.
codex.quest.end_apotheosis.codex.text.1: Beyond — what no mod foresaw and what's possible from their parts. That's your book now.
codex.quest.end_apotheosis.codex.title: Codex Closed
codex.quest.end_apotheosis.darkness_unah: Unahzaal in Eternal Darkness. The Calamity Ring is the proof.
codex.quest.end_apotheosis.seven.text.0: Factory gauge, excavator, antimatter, million-slot vault, level-five colony, Lamp of Cinders, Ultimate World. Not to turn in — to show.
codex.quest.end_apotheosis.seven.title: Seven Peaks
codex.quest.end_marathon.antimatter64.te: Sixty-four antimatter pellets. An SPS running a week on a fusion reactor. This isn't a game anymore, it's physics.
codex.quest.end_marathon.circuits256.tex: Atomic alloy in industrial amounts. Without fivefold ore and twenty-deep autocrafting it's impossible.
One crystal of every Eternal Tales dimension — all nine, turned in at once. It means you can return anywhere at any moment. Which means you can give them up.
codex.quest.end_marathon.crystals9.title: Nine Worlds in a Pocket
codex.quest.end_marathon.mech1024.text.0: One thousand twenty-four precision mechanisms. One crafter line gives one every few seconds; count how many lines you need.
codex.quest.end_marathon.mech1024.title: A Thousand Mechanisms
One thousand twenty-four advanced processors. A network that makes itself.
Four thousand ninety-six IE steel ingots. An arc furnace on a diesel grid — the only realistic path.
codex.quest.end_marathon.steel4096.title: Four Thousand Steel
codex.quest.end_monuments.bridge.text.0: Two thousand forty-eight tracks. A line from base to colony, colony to mine, mine to the airship pier. A train circling for half an hour.
codex.quest.end_monuments.bridge.title: Bridge Across the World
codex.quest.end_monuments.cathedral.text: Two thousand blocks through the architect's cutter — any, but not vanilla. Domum Ornamentum makes them from anything; only patience matters. The book accepts timber frame: one thousand twenty-four panels.
codex.quest.end_monuments.eternal_town.t: Five hundred twelve Ultimate Bricks. Rebuild Eternal Town from a material only the Arkemers make.
Eight nethersteel screw breeches and one hundred twenty-eight HE shells. A fortress that isn't taken.
codex.quest.end_monuments.fortress.title: Bastion
codex.quest.end_monuments.matrix.text.0: Fifty-four casings and eight ultimate induction cells. A battery that outlives a fusion reactor.
codex.quest.end_monuments.matrix.title: Matrix
Two hundred fifty-six pearlescent levitite and sixty-four smart propellers. That's what it takes to lift something the size of a colony.
codex.quest.end_monuments.shipyard.title: Shipyard
codex.quest.end_monuments.spire.text.0: One thousand twenty-four Create metal girders. A tower of them is visible from the next chunk, if Distant Horizons doesn't lie.
codex.quest.end_monuments.spire.title: Spire
codex.quest.end_monuments.vault_city.tex: Sixteen 64k disks. A million slots. A network enough for everything you'll ever mine.
codex.quest.et_amber.crystal_amb.title: Amber Crystal
codex.quest.et_amber.enter_amb.title: Amber Lands
codex.quest.et_amber.greatness.text.0: And the pharos — a beacon. Both into the Amber crystal.
codex.quest.et_amber.greatness.title: Crystal of Greatness
codex.quest.et_amber.keybekium.text.0: The metal forged into weapons for the invasion of Eden.
codex.quest.et_amber.keybekium.title: Daredian
codex.quest.et_amber.maze.text.0: A royal secret under lock. The key — in the kingdom itself, with those who don't want it found.
codex.quest.et_amber.maze.title: Amber Labyrinth
codex.quest.et_amber.smuciel.title: Smuciel
True power. Armor and brush — best of their kind.
codex.quest.et_amber.truadamantite.title: Truadamantite
codex.quest.et_amber.xaxxas.text.0: Prepare for war. The ruler of Amber — the last boss of normal progression.
codex.quest.et_amber.xaxxas.title: Xaxxas XIX
codex.quest.et_archaeology.blueprints.te: From the ground come plans for weapons nobody makes anymore: Ammit's staff, archangel's wings, the bloody anchor.
codex.quest.et_archaeology.brush.text.0: Venetium — the start; truadamantite — the limit. Suspicious blocks wait in every world.
codex.quest.et_archaeology.brush.title: Brushes
Ruby, topaz, corundum, amber. Quality — from the magnifying glass, sandpaper and the archery skill. Gloves and rings here too.
codex.quest.et_archaeology.jewelry.title: Jewelry Table
codex.quest.et_archaeology.rings.text.0: Lycanthropy, harpy, crimson tears, Hircine. Into accessory slots.
codex.quest.et_archaeology.rings.title: Rings
codex.quest.et_archaeology.sherds.text.0: From sherds — neodymium and uranium vases. Uranium ones glow, and not as a joke.
codex.quest.et_archaeology.sherds.title: Sherds and Vases
codex.quest.et_archaeology.shredder.text: Takes a blueprint apart and teaches you by it. The Arkemer one is better.
codex.quest.et_archaeology.totems.text.0: Blessings of the gods on a permanent basis.
codex.quest.et_archaeology.totems.title: Ceramic Totems
